title: Pilot accelerator — 1-week surge playbook
content:
Context:
This is a compact, pragmatic playbook intended to convert a customer trial (pilot) into a meaningful production evaluation within 1 calendar week. The target customer is a mid-market SaaS product team with an existing REST backend and a test dataset of ~20k documents. The goal: deliver an end-to-end hosted-api POC that validates latency, cost profile, and quality for two integration flows (chat widget + content tagging pipeline).

High-level objectives (end of week):
- Working prototype: chat widget integrated with Redwood hosted API against redwood/llama-2-13b-like model variant (or customer-approved equivalent).
- Batch tagging pipeline that processes 2k docs/hour with acceptable accuracy baseline and cost estimate.
- Latency & cost smoke tests run; initial dashboard + cost-per-100k-token estimate.
- Acceptance checklist signed by customer PM and SE.

Kickoff (Day 0 — remote, 60 min)
- Attendees: customer PM, customer Eng lead, Redwood SE, Solutions PM, Infra lead (optional).
- Agenda: intro goals, constraints, data availability, success metrics, sandbox account access, timeline, handoffs.
- Outputs: agreed acceptance criteria, data access path, cloud creds (if needed), Slack channel and meeting cadence.

Day-by-day plan:
Day 1 — Setup & data onboarding- Confirm test account and API keys (hosted sandbox).- Ingest sample dataset (2k documents) into a temporary storage bucket.- Schema map: fields used for tagging and chat context.- Quick smoke: run 50 sample queries through API to validate connection and tokens.

Day 2 — Chat widget integration (MVP)- Provide lightweight React widget snippet; instrumented for request timing and token counts.- Implement server-side proxy to attach API key and session management.- Validate streaming response behavior; fallback path for timeouts.- Log format agreed (request id, user id, model, token counts, latency).

Day 3 — Batch tagging pipeline & quant baseline- Create small batch worker (Python/Beam or simple multiprocessing) to process 500 docs/hour locally.- Define tagging taxonomy and prompt templates; run against 200-sample holdout.- Produce baseline precision/recall at current prompt; save prompts for eval harness.- Start cost estimation jobs with detailed token counting.

Day 4 — Load & latency testing- Run synthetic traffic for chat integration: 50 concurrent users for 10 minutes.- Capture p95/p99 latencies, error rates, and token throughput.- Stress batch pipeline to 2k/hr target; watch memory/CPU and observe model-level throttling.- If p95 exceeds SLO, try immediate mitigations: shorter context window, prefix caching, smaller model variant.

Day 5 — Consolidation & acceptance- Prepare short demo (10–15 min) and run through acceptance checklist.- Deliver initial metrics dashboard (latency by route, cost breakdown, success rate of tagging).- Walk through operational runbooks for support: who to call if token burn, quota hit, or model rollback needed.

Acceptance checklist (customer sign-off)
- Chat flow end-to-end demo works with < 600ms median latency for cached prefix, p95 < 2s for user interactions in hosted sandbox.
- Batch tagging pipeline processes 2k docs/hour and achieves >= baseline F1 agreed in kickoff.
- Observability: request-level logs land in customer sandbox logs (or Redwood demo dashboard) with required fields.
- Cost estimate: per-100k-token cost and an extrapolated monthly run rate presented.

Task tracker (owner, ETA, status notes)
- Sandbox API key provisioning — Daniel — Day 0 — pending
- Sample data ingestion — Asha — Day 1 — in-progress (need schema clarification)- React widget snippet + proxy sample — Marco — Day 2 — ready (needs customer styling)- Tagging prompt templates + eval set — Priya — Day 3 — drafting (2 variants)- Synthetic load scripts + metrics capture — Sofia — Day 4 — queued

Risk register & mitigations
- Data privacy constraints: customer may not permit sample records in external bucket. Mitigation: use obfuscated/synth data or offer Private deployment eval.
- Quota or burst limits on hosted sandbox causing false negatives. Mitigation: coordinate with infra to lift quotas for the week and document limits.
- Model quality below expectation on long-tail docs. Mitigation: create targeted prompt tuning and fallback classifier.
- Unexpected memory/CPU spikes on batch worker. Mitigation: cap concurrency, profiling, and move to dedicated runner.

Operational playbook snippets
- Rollback policy: if p95 latency > 3x target for >10 minutes, automated fallback to smaller model variant and alert SE channel.- Escalation matrix: Redwood SE -> Solutions PM -> Infra oncall. Contact: solutions-oncall@redwood.ai (internal).

Open questions / decisions to make- Does the customer want persistent session caching across widget reloads? (affects KV cache design)- Are there regulatory redaction requirements for chat transcripts?- Confirm preferred cost granularity: per-token vs per-conversation?

Quick list of helpful links and artifacts- Sandbox dashboard for customer: https://console.redwood.ai/sandbox/quickview/PL-5432- Example widget repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pilot-widget- Eval harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/tree/pilot

Notes to self (SE tips)
- Keep prompts shallow and explicit for tagging tasks; avoid open-ended formulations in the first pass.- Instrument token counts at both request and model response to estimate costs precisely.- Pre-create a small canary model variant with lower context length for emergency fallback.

Next steps (immediate)
- Daniel to send kickoff calendar invite and Slack channel (within 2 hours).- Asha to upload 200-sample anonymized dataset and confirm field mapping (EOD Day 1).
- Marco to drop initial widget snippet into the shared repo and open PR for styling adjustments (Day 2).

End of playbook — keep this short doc as the single source during the week; expand into a more formal POC report if pilot moves to dedicated evaluation.
